name: workers
description: Two side panes. Git: each folder directly inside the session's folder with the git branch checked out in it, or "no git"; /git opens it. Workers: the project's chats, who is working on what, which step, how long, and whose turn it is; /workers opens it. The app's own notes in a prompt (system reminders, side-session events, messages from another chat) are never filed as the person's instructions. A chat in the list also takes what the person answered for it on the worker board and types it in as their own words, and tells the board why one could not be typed. An answer that ends with a "For you" block the chat filed no ask for has its items filed on the board when the turn ends. After the turn in which a worker reported its step it is compacted when large (list.json "compactAbove", 250000 tokens unless set, 0 for never) or, with list.json "afterStep": "clear", cleared with /clear even when more work follows: the worker board first keeps the conversation as a log, the card moves to the new session, and the fresh conversation is told who it is, where its rules and log are, its open instructions, and to run work next. The main chat and the partners are never cleared; they are compacted at rest above the threshold. Each call of the work tool carries a request id, so a call whose answer is slow or cut off is asked again and recorded once; a board that does not answer is named with its reason, and a take it does not answer within 15 s is given up and asked again. When the person pauses all chats on the board, each chat is told at its next batch of tool calls to write its checkpoint and end its turn; after the resume the main chat is told whom to wake, and each chat holding a step its checkpoint. A chat renamed in the app follows the name the board shows it under: refused under its old name, it joins under the new one and asks once more. The chat the list names "supervisor" reads the board's health summary (work health) and files incidents (work incident), and is cleared after every turn of its own, without a log, so each sweep starts empty. Every call to the board says the mod's version, so the board sees a chat on an older mod, and each chat writes it on its card: the Workers pane shows each chat's version and, for one older than the newest, that the board has it restarted after its step. A worker whose last report is newer than its last clear is cleared when the board names it at a take (the log refused while background work ran, a restart or a pause between). Each chat tells the board its turn state, busy, idle (with background work still running or not) or asking the person, the moment it changes and with every take, so the board shows what the chat says instead of guessing; while a clear is on its way the report still goes every 5 s. The board hands out every task itself (its redesign's Part 2): the work tool has no queue, requeue or unqueue. A chat learns its name from the board by its session id (the app's title is not needed): at its start and before a prompt, at most once a minute, it asks the board who its session is and joins under that name; a card the board names under another session (a worker cleared in a new process) is moved to the chat's own session, a worker with the words of a clear. Every 20 s a chat in the list claims the board's hand jobs and does them by code, with no model turn: where the app allows its code the send-message tool with no question (an allow rule; a chat in Auto mode has its sends put to the classifier, which denies them, so without the rule it says so and gets none), it starts, wakes and resumes chats with it and, where the app allows its code both set tools with no question (an allow rule), sets a chat's model and effort with them, restarts an idle worker for a new mod (closes and reopens it) and starts a new worker by running the stored start-worker task and looks the plan's limits up when the board's newest reading is old, and takes a worker the person removed off the list and closes its chat; a worker whose task the person stops or that is removed is told at its next tool call; it says what it did. A popup that may wait for the person shows on the board: a call that does not run long by itself (not a shell, subagent or wait) still running after a minute is filed on the board as an ask in the chat's name, in a few plain words (answered in its chat), and the chat reports itself asking, until the call goes on or its turn ends. The mod uses no classic hooks (the app's guard skips them on a work login), so both logins behave the same.
